name: Camera Angles
entries: low angle: the view looks upward from below the main subjects, showing their undersides and the space above them
high angle: the view looks downward from above the main subjects, showing their upper surfaces and the ground around them
Dutch angle: the view is rolled sideways so the horizon is diagonal, without tilting the subjects' physical supports
eye-level angle: the view meets the main subjects at their eye height, without looking up or down at them
ground-level angle: the view looks across the ground from beside the subjects' feet or bases, with foreground surfaces prominent
overhead angle: the view looks straight down onto the main subjects and the layout around them
waist-level angle: the view looks horizontally across the subjects at the height of their middle, keeping vertical supports upright
raised oblique angle: the view looks diagonally down from one side, revealing both the fronts and upper surfaces of the main subjects
